---
title: "Using sideview with a screen reader"
description: >
  The list view, plain-sentence results and keyboard use, for screen reader and keyboard users.
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(sideview)
```

sideview was first built as a visual canvas. Since 0.8.0 it also has a **list view** that reads top to bottom, and its
checks print as plain sentences in the console. This page says how to use both.

## How well is this tested

sideview 0.8.0 is **checked with automated WCAG tests (axe) and real-browser keyboard tests; an NVDA script is written
but has not yet been run; not yet tested by blind users.** Please treat it as a first step and tell us where it fails
(see "Report a problem" below).

## Start in the list view

The list view shows the same tables as text in one column. Start in it with the `view` argument or an option:

```{r list-view, eval = FALSE}
# for one call
sideview(patients, visits, view = "list")

# for the whole session
options(sideview.view = "list")
```

You can also press the **List view** button in the toolbar at any time. Switching is announced ("List view" or
"Canvas view") and focus moves to the first heading of the list.

The single-key shortcuts of the canvas (F, T, D and so on) can get in the way of a screen reader. They default to off in
the list view. Turn them off everywhere with the "Keyboard shortcuts" switch in the `?` list, or at the start with:

```{r shortcuts, eval = FALSE}
options(sideview.shortcuts = FALSE)
```

`Ctrl+K` and `Ctrl+Enter` always work.

## A reading tour by headings

In the list view, move by headings (H in NVDA and JAWS, or the rotor in VoiceOver). The headings are:

1. **Summary**: counts of tables, join steps and pipeline steps, whether code is ready, skip links, Save, Open and the
   keyboard shortcuts switch.
2. **Tables**: one heading per table, for example "labs, 5,000 rows by 3 columns, full table." Under it, one line per
   column (name, label, kind, and the distinct and missing counts) with Sort, Filter and Inspect buttons, then the rows
   as a captioned table, 25 a page, with Previous rows, Next rows and Go to row. A page change is announced
   ("Rows 26 to 50 of 5,000.") and focus stays on the button.
3. **Join**: pick two tables and their key columns, read the join check as sentences, and add the join.
4. **Merge SUPP**: for a SUPP-- table, check and add the merge into its parent.
5. **Transform**: sort, filter, rename and the other steps.
6. **Pipeline**: the steps so far, each of which you can switch off, move or delete.
7. **Code**: the generated R code, with Copy and Insert.
8. **Copilot**: present only when a language model is set up.

What you do in the list view makes the same code as the canvas does, and a join made on the canvas shows in the list
view's Pipeline.

## Results as sentences in the console

The results of the checks print as sentences, not as lists of numbers. For example:

```{r sentences, eval = FALSE}
chk <- sv_join_diagnostics(patients, visits, by = "patient_id")
chk                       # "Join of patients and visits by patient_id is one to many. ..."

sv_column_profile(patients, "age")
sv_supp_check(ae, suppae)
sv_detect_discrepancies(patients, "sex")
sv_suggest_mappings(patients, visits)

unclass(chk)              # the raw list, if you want the numbers
```

`sv_describe()` writes one sentence for each table and one line for each column. It is the text twin of looking at the
cards:

```{r describe}
patients <- data.frame(
  id  = 1:6,
  sex = c("M", "F", "F", NA, "M", "F"),
  age = c(40, 51, 62, 38, 45, 29)
)
sv_describe(patients)
```

A large duckdb or Arrow table is described from its summaries and is never loaded into memory.

## Use a browser, not the RStudio pane

For a screen reader we recommend the gadget in a real browser:

```{r browser, eval = FALSE}
sideview(patients, visits, viewer = "browser", view = "list")
```

The reason is what the tests can and cannot show. The keyboard and axe tests run in a real browser, where the page has
full keyboard and assistive-technology support. How the RStudio Viewer pane and the RStudio dialog pass keys and speech
to a screen reader has **not been measured**: we have not yet read them with a screen reader, so we make no claim about
them. Until that is done, use `viewer = "browser"`. The saved HTML widget (`save_sideview()`) opens in a browser too.

## Report a problem

If something is not read, is read wrongly or cannot be reached by keyboard, please
[open an accessibility issue](https://github.com/lauyeehow1986-hub/sideview/issues/new?template=accessibility-feedback.yml).
Tell us your screen reader and its version, the browser or RStudio pane, what you did and what you heard.
